explanation: TeX only allows one `^` directly on a base, and this line has two — `x^1^2` does not say whether the second `^` attaches to `x` or to `1`. If both parts belong in one superscript together, group them: `x^{1,2}`. If a `^` was meant as ordinary text rather than a script, wrap it in `\text{}` instead.
title: Two superscripts on the same base
